name: Artesian Resources Corporation
business_overview: Artesian Resources Corporation provides water, wastewater, and other services in Delaware, Maryland, and Pennsylvania. The company distributes and sells water to residential, commercial, industrial, governmental, municipal, and utility customers, as well as for public and private fire protection; and offers wastewater collection, treatment infrastructure, and wastewater services to customers. It also provides contract water and wastewater operations; water, sewer, and internal service line protection plans; and wastewater management services, as well as design, construction, and engineering services. In addition, the company offers services to other water utilities; owns real estate properties, including land for office buildings, a water treatment plant, and wastewater facility; and provides design, installation, maintenance, and repair services. As of December 31, 2025, it served customers in Delaware, Maryland, and Pennsylvania through 1,515 miles of transmission and distribution mains. Artesian Resources Corporation was founded in 1905 and is headquartered in Newark, Delaware.

classification_meta.logic_summary: Regulated water utility providing water and wastewater services in the Mid-Atlantic US.

Infrastructure investment continues to enhance service reliability, though the company’s concentrated Delaware footprint means regulatory outcomes carry outsized weight. The defensive, non-discretionary nature of water utility services provides a buffer against an uncertain macro backdrop marked by Fed policy recalibration. Market sentiment shows technical strength (share price crossing above its 200-day moving average), balanced by a modest analyst downgrade, keeping the outlook cautiously positive.

**Management strategy and execution:** Leadership is prioritizing a constructive regulatory outcome in the Delaware rate case and sustained capital spending on system improvements, aiming to translate these into modest earnings growth. The company maintains a long track record of reliable dividend increases, reinforcing its identity as a steady income compounder. The narrative around execution is steady and conservative, with capital allocation focused on infrastructure and shareholder returns rather than transformative moves, preserving credibility with income-oriented investors who value consistency.

# Arta Market Brief - July 2026: Markets Meet the New Fed

July 09, 2026

Written by Brandon Ho, CFA, Head of Investment Advisory SG

Commentary as of 8 July 2026

Kevin Warsh has said he wants to run the Fed the way Alan Greenspan did, though so far that comparison looks like it is about style rather than stance. His debut as Fed Chair sounded hawkish, not dovish, sending yields higher and knocking equities off their highs. Then a short lived reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a sharp drop in oil prices and a soft June jobs report all eased the pressure on the Fed to hike, undoing much of that within weeks. Markets are still sizing up the new Fed chair, and if Greenspan really is the model, it may say more about how much he talks than about which way rates are headed.
